title: Transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis study utilizing streamlined referral pathways with education, cardiac AI echocardiography, and point-of-care testing
official: ATTR Amyloidosis: Study of utilizing streamlined referral pathways with education, cardiac Al echocardiography and point-of-care testing - a multicentre stepped-wedge, cluster, non-randomised implementation study
summary:
Background and study aims
Transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTR amyloidosis) is a condition in which an abnormal protein builds up in the heart and other organs, causing heart failure. It can be treated, but its symptoms are easily mistaken for more common conditions. As a result, people currently wait almost two years between first having heart symptoms and getting a diagnosis. Earlier diagnosis means treatment can start sooner. This study aims to find out whether a faster referral pathway helps people with suspected ATTR amyloidosis reach a specialist diagnosis sooner. The new pathway combines training for clinic staff with a heart ultrasound scan (echocardiogram) taken on a handheld device and analysed by approved artificial intelligence (AI) software. If the AI result suggests amyloidosis, the patient is fast-tracked to the Liverpool Amyloidosis Diagnostic Hub. A clinician always reviews the result and makes all care decisions.

Who can participate?
Adults aged 50 years or over who attend heart failure, cardiology, care of the elderly, neurology or carpal tunnel clinics at participating NHS sites in Cheshire, Merseyside and the North West of England, and who have warning signs of ATTR amyloidosis.

What does the study involve?
About 10 participating clinics all start by using the usual referral pathway. Every four months, two clinics switch to the new pathway, in a pre-planned order, until all have switched. This takes 24 months in total. About half of the participants will be seen under each pathway. Taking part involves the usual clinic assessment and a short quality of life questionnaire. People seen under the new pathway also have an extra ultrasound scan with a handheld device, lasting about 15 minutes. Six months later, the research team repeats the questionnaire by telephone or post and checks medical records for diagnosis, treatment and hospital admissions. There are no extra hospital visits.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participants may benefit from earlier specialist assessment, diagnosis or treatment, although this cannot be guaranteed. The information collected may help improve referral pathways for future patients. The extra scan is painless, although pressure from the probe may cause brief discomfort. Routine blood tests may cause brief discomfort or bruising. Some people may feel anxious while waiting for results. Tests may also reveal unexpected findings; these will be managed by the clinical team as part of usual care.

Where is the study run from?
The University of Liverpool (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
February 2027 to July 2029

Who is funding the study?
AstraZeneca (UK)

Who is the main contact?
Dr Rajiv Sankaranarayanan, Rajiv.Sankaranarayanan@liverpool.ac.uk
conditions: Transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis, including transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), in adults with red-flag features of the condition

interventions.name: Us2.ai (Us2.v2) AI echocardiography analysis software (Eko.ai Pte Ltd), GE Vscan Air handheld ultrasound

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Aged 50 years or over
2. Referred to a heart failure diagnostic clinic, cardiology clinic, or care of the elderly, carpal tunnel or neurology outpatient clinic at a participating site
3. At least one red flag suggestive of ATTR amyloidosis:
3.1. Cardiac: postural hypotension; intolerance of RAAS inhibitors or beta-blockers for HFrEF because of hypotension; paradoxical low-flow low-gradient aortic stenosis
3.2. Multisystem: autonomic dysfunction, bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, lumbar spinal stenosis, ruptured biceps tendon, alternating diarrhoea and constipation
3.3. Cardiac tests: NT-proBNP >3000 ng/L; discordance between ECG voltage and left ventricular wall thickness where interventricular septal thickness is ≥12 mm
4. Able to give written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Cognitive impairment or inability to give informed consent
2. Unable to be referred to the Liverpool Amyloidosis Diagnostic Hub
3. Life-limiting condition with expected prognosis under 1 year (e.g. end-stage heart failure, metastatic malignancy, end-stage COPD)
4. Chronic kidney disease stage 5 or on haemodialysis
